reason: The sources provide multiple independent cross-verifications across five separate sites for dimensions, formation, volcanic features, and discovery of Valles Marineris.
story: In 1971, NASA's Mariner 9 arrived at Mars and unveiled a geological behemoth: Valles Marineris. Stretching roughly 4,000 kilometers along the Martian equator, this vast rupture is the largest canyon system in the Solar System. If placed on Earth, it would span across the continental United States from New York to California. Unlike the Grand Canyon, which was carved by river erosion, Valles Marineris was ripped open by tectonic forces when the nearby Tharsis volcanic bulge surged upward billions of years ago, pulling Mars's crust apart. Its chasms plunge up to 7 kilometers deep, easily swallowing Earth's highest peaks, and were widened over time by catastrophic landslides. Even more astonishing, inside this immense canyon floor, scientists have identified young volcanic cones dating back only 200 to 400 million years, alongside relict glacier ice and a newly discovered 9,000-meter-tall volcano at its western gateway.
angle: Mars hosts a tectonic canyon so colossal that it would stretch across the entire continental United States and drop four to five times deeper than the Grand Canyon.

claims.claim: Valles Marineris is the largest canyon system in the Solar System.
Valles Marineris stretches approximately 4,000 kilometers in length.
Valles Marineris spans about 200 kilometers in width.
The canyon system plunges to depths of up to 7 kilometers.
The canyon system is located along or near the equator of Mars.
Valles Marineris lies directly east of the Tharsis volcanic region.
Valles Marineris was discovered and imaged by NASA's Mariner 9 spacecraft in the early 1970s.
The canyon system formed primarily by tectonic rifting and crustal extension linked to the uplift of Tharsis.
Massive landslides collapsed canyon walls and contributed to widening Valles Marineris over time.
The canyon system starts in the west at the fractured terrain of Noctis Labyrinthus.
Valles Marineris contains parallel western troughs named Ius Chasma and Tithonium Chasma.
The central region of Valles Marineris includes Melas Chasma, Candor Chasma, and Ophir Chasma.
At its eastern end, Valles Marineris connects to outflow channels that empty into the Chryse basin.
Coprates Chasma contains a field of volcanic cones dated to between 200 and 400 million years ago.
A deeply eroded giant volcano standing over 9,000 meters tall was identified at Eastern Noctis Labyrinthus near the canyon's western rim.
Evidence of buried glacier ice and sulfate deposits exists near the base of the newly identified Noctis volcano.
The European Space Agency's Mars Express orbiter imaged Valles Marineris using its High Resolution Stereo Camera.
Valles Marineris is roughly ten times longer and several times deeper than Earth's Grand Canyon.

disputed: Canyon length estimates differ slightly between sources, with S1, S2, and S5 stating approximately 4,000 km while S3 cites around 3,000 km; scripts should describe it as 'up to 4,000 kilometers long'.

The exact origin of the interior layered deposits in canyons like Candor and Coprates remains debated between lakebed sedimentation, volcanic ash accumulation, and aeolian dust; scripts should present these as competing hypotheses.
The origin of the small cones in Coprates Chasma was previously contested between mud volcanism and magmatic cinder cones; scripts should attribute magmatic rock volcanism to recent MRO studies.
